title: Understanding inspection modes
content:
## Overview

FortiGate web filtering helps stop infections from malware sites and prevent communication if an infection occurs. After a TCP connection is established, the user requests the content of a specific website using an HTTP GET request. FortiGate checks the HTTP GET request and sends a real-time request to the FortiGuard servers to determine the category of the website. Based on the category information from the FortiGuard Distribution Network (FDN), FortiGate performs a specific action based on the profile applied to the policy.

In FortiOS, there are three main components of web filtering:

- **Web content filtering**: blocks web pages containing words or patterns that you specify.
- **URL filtering**: uses URLs and URL patterns to block or exempt web pages from specific sources, or block malicious URLs discovered by FortiSandbox.
- **FortiGuard Web Filtering service**: provides many additional categories you can use to filter web traffic.

![Understanding inspection modes](diagram:0)

## SSL Certificate Inspection

For encrypted protocols, FortiGate requires additional inspection. When using SSL certificate inspection, FortiGate inspects the headers up to only the SSL/TLS layer. FortiGate does not decrypt or inspect any encrypted traffic — it inspects only the initial unencrypted SSL handshake.

During the TLS handshake, the Client Hello message includes the Server Name Indication (SNI). If the SNI field exists, FortiGate uses it to obtain the FQDN to rate the site. If the SNI is not present, FortiGate retrieves the FQDN from the CN field of the server certificate.

In some cases, the CN server name might not match the requested FQDN. For example, the common name (CN) field in the digital certificate of youtube.com is google.com. So, if FortiGate uses SSL certificate inspection and the browser does not support SNI, FortiGate may incorrectly categorize the site.

## Flow-Based vs. Proxy-Based Inspection

You can configure web filtering in **flow-based** or **proxy-based** inspection mode.

**Flow-based inspection** examines the file as it passes through FortiGate, without buffering it. Packets are analyzed and forwarded as they are received, without waiting for the complete file or web page.

Advantages of flow-based inspection mode:

- The user sees a faster response time for HTTP requests compared to proxy-based inspection mode.
- There is less chance of a time-out error caused by the server at the other end responding slowly.
- From FortiOS 7.4.4 and later, flow-based web filter profiling supports safe search and restrictions on YouTube and Vimeo access.

Disadvantages of flow-based inspection mode:

- A number of security features available in proxy-based inspection mode are not available in flow-based mode.
- Fewer actions are available based on the categorization of the website by FortiGuard services.

**Proxy-based inspection** refers to a transparent proxy. FortiGate buffers traffic and examines it as a whole before determining an action. Because FortiGate examines the data as a whole, it can examine more points of data than in flow-based inspection. The proxy analyzes the headers and may change them, such as HTTP host and URL, for web filtering. If a security profile decides to block the connection, the proxy can send a replacement message to the client. This adds latency to the overall transmission speed.

Make sure that both an SSL inspection profile (such as the certificate-inspection profile) and a web filter profile are selected in the associated firewall policy.
